AknSource.description:
One upstream that yields documents convertible to AKN.

Distinct from `SourceAdapter`, the acquisition substrate keyed by adapter kind:
this is a format-and-protocol pairing declared in `config.json#akn_sources`.
Both coexist during the schema migration and `effective_tier` walks both; legacy
configs without `format`/`protocol` default to PDF over HTTP.

auth_env_var.description: Name of the environment variable holding the credential. The credential itself is never stored in the config.
auth_env_var.title: Auth Env Var

auth_scheme.description: How requests to the source are authenticated.
auth_scheme.title: Auth Scheme

coverage.description: How much of the statute base the source holds.
coverage.title: Coverage

description.description: Free-text description of the source, often including its provenance.
description.title: Description

fallback_format.description: The format still available when the source's credential is unset, so `effective_tier` can count it at that format.
fallback_format.title: Fallback Format

format.description: The format the source serves, which sets its tier in `effective_tier`. Defaults to PDF.
format.title: Format

protocol.description: How documents are fetched from the source. Defaults to HTTP.
protocol.title: Protocol

requires_token.description: True for a source that needs an access token: `effective_tier` skips it when the token's environment variable is unset, unless `fallback_format` declares a usable downgrade.
requires_token.title: Requires Token

schema_id.description: Identifier of the schema the source's documents follow.
schema_id.title: Schema Id

schema_url.description: URL of the schema the source's documents follow.
schema_url.title: Schema Url

url_template.description: URL of the source, or a template for one document's URL.
url_template.title: Url Template

AknSource.title: AknSource

amending_body_structure.description: Body shape of an amending instrument. `two_pasal_roman`: the host instrument numbers its own articles in Roman numerals, so an Arabic-numbered article after them is quoted amending text.
amending_body_structure.title: Amending Body Structure

amendment_item_kind.description: Hierarchy element that numbers each amendment an amending article makes. What follows it belongs to the amended statute, so it does not compete in the host's numbering; empty leaves the pass inert.
amendment_item_kind.title: Amendment Item Kind

cross_reference_format.description: How amendments cite the provisions they change. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
cross_reference_format.title: Cross Reference Format

phrasing.description: A phrase that marks a paragraph as an amendment instruction, in addition to the built-in English cues, so its references are classed as amendments.
phrasing.title: Phrasing

style.description: How the jurisdiction drafts amendments. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
style.title: Style

trigger_phrases.description: Lead-in phrases marking an embedded amendment article: a number following one of these plus a colon is quoted content, not a new top-level article.
trigger_phrases.title: Trigger Phrases

AttachmentCaption.description:
A caption line opening an attachment. AKN models a schedule and a
mandatory companion alike, so legal force is declared per caption.

always_opens.description: True where no table in the body carries this caption, so a line that opens with it always begins the attachment.
always_opens.title: Always Opens

caption.description: Caption that opens the attachment. Captions are centred in the source, so the match tolerates a wide indent.
caption.title: Caption

hierarchy.description: Levels the attachment's own content uses, since an annex can be a lettered outline rather than the article hierarchy of its body. Empty uses the body's levels, or none.
hierarchy.title: Hierarchy

normative.description: False for an attachment with no normative force, such as an explanatory memorandum, which cannot serve as a legal basis.
normative.title: Normative

prefix.description: True where the caption opens a longer title on the same line ("SCHEDULE of fees…"), so the caption need only begin the line. The line is the heading.
prefix.title: Prefix

AttachmentCaption.title: AttachmentCaption

BindingRegime.description:
Non-membership binding regime, treaty frameworks, bilateral regimes,
constitutional annexes. Used for instruments that are legally binding on a
jurisdiction but are not memberships in an international organisation.

code.description: Code of the regime, canonicalised against the supranational body registry.
code.title: Code

direct_effect.description: How strongly the regime's instruments take effect, from override to none.
direct_effect.title: Direct Effect

in_force_from.description: Date the regime took effect, as an ISO date.
in_force_from.title: In Force From

in_force_until.description: Date the regime ends or ended, as an ISO date.
in_force_until.title: In Force Until

kind.description: What kind of regime it is.
kind.title: Kind

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

renewable.description: Whether the regime can be renewed.
renewable.title: Renewable

reporting_cadence.description: How often the regime requires reports.
reporting_cadence.title: Reporting Cadence

superseded_subjects.description: Subject areas where the regime's rules displace domestic law.
superseded_subjects.title: Superseded Subjects

territories.description: Territorial scope, typically set for UN Security Council resolutions and other time-bounded regimes; absent for permanent treaty frameworks.
territories.title: Territories

BindingRegime.title: BindingRegime

CalendarConversion.description:
Deterministic conversion rule for non-Gregorian local calendars.

kind selects which optional fields apply:

- epoch_offset  single-epoch calendars. Gregorian = local_year + epoch_year,
                where epoch_year is an integer offset (Buddhist Era -543).
- era_table     named era segments with boundaries.
- hijri_lunar   Lunar calendar, ~354 days. Needs codify.calendar, not an offset.
- hijri_solar   Solar calendar, Gregorian year length.
- ethiopian     ~7-8 year offset, 13-month year.
- buddhist      Buddhist Era calendar, epoch_year -543.
- bikram_samvat 57-year offset, month-sensitive (Chaitra straddles the
                mid-April new year).

date_cues.description: Phrases that introduce the date a document was made. A dated line elsewhere in the text is some other instrument's.
date_cues.title: Date Cues

epoch_year.description: Integer added to the local year to give the Gregorian year (for example -543 for the Buddhist calendar, or 1911 where year 1 is 1912 CE). None for calendars without a fixed offset, such as hijri, ethiopian, era_table and bikram_samvat.
epoch_year.title: Epoch Year

eras.description: Era table for an era-based calendar, for example [{"name": "Reiwa", "start": "2019-05-01"}].
eras.title: Eras

kind.description: Which conversion applies; it selects the optional fields that are read.
kind.title: Kind

month_day_is_gregorian.description: Whether the months and days coincide with the Gregorian ones, so only the year converts. False for any calendar with a grid of its own.
month_day_is_gregorian.title: Month Day Is Gregorian

month_names.description: Month names in the local calendar's own order, index 0 = month 1. Present only where a dated line is read off the source text.
month_names.title: Month Names

new_year_day.description: Day of `new_year_month` on which the local year begins, for month-sensitive conversions. Unset means the first of the month.
new_year_day.title: New Year Day

new_year_month.description: Gregorian month in which the local year begins, for conversions that depend on the month (Bikram Samvat begins in mid-April).
new_year_month.title: New Year Month

new_year_reform_year.description: First local year that began on 1 January. Before it the year began in `new_year_month`, so a date in an earlier month falls in the next Gregorian year.
new_year_reform_year.title: New Year Reform Year

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

offset.description: For month-sensitive conversions: the years to subtract from the local year before the new-year day; on or after it, `offset + 1`.
offset.title: Offset

year_particles.description: Words marking a year as belonging to this calendar ("B.E.", "A.H.").
year_particles.title: Year Particles

CalendarConversion.title: CalendarConversion

ClassificationRule.description:
Deterministic rule for assigning a document class from the incoming header or
metadata. Tried in descending priority; the first match wins. No match falls back to
`default_document_class` and to whatever heuristics `StructuringConfig.prompt_additions`
still carries.

signal          what `pattern` is tested against
  date_range      nothing; the match is `date_from`/`date_until` alone, for laws
                  post-dating a regime change
  preamble_match  the preamble or enacting-formula text
  issuer_role     the enacting body's role (for example a head of state or a cabinet)
  gazette_series  the official gazette series the document was published in
  title_regex     the document title (a fixed prefix such as "Regulation:")

date_from.description: First document date the rule applies to, inclusive. A rule with a date bound is skipped for a document without a date.
date_from.title: Date From

date_until.description: Last document date the rule applies to, inclusive.
date_until.title: Date Until

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

pattern.description: Regex tested against the signal's text. Unused for `date_range`.
pattern.title: Pattern

pattern_flags.description: Regex flags for `pattern`, for example "i" for case-insensitive matching.
pattern_flags.title: Pattern Flags

priority.description: Rules are tried from highest priority to lowest; the first match wins.
priority.title: Priority

signal.description: Which part of the document `pattern` is tested against.
signal.title: Signal

target_document_class.description: The document class assigned when the rule matches. It must be a key of `document_classes`.
target_document_class.title: Target Document Class

ClassificationRule.title: ClassificationRule

max_total.description: Most documents one discovery run returns, unless the caller sets a limit.
max_total.title: Max Total

output.description: Path of the basket file discovery writes, relative to the repository root.
output.title: Output

queries.description: Discovery query per doctype, in the portal's own query syntax.
queries.title: Queries

DiscoveryConfig.title: DiscoveryConfig

amendment_markers.description: The pair of strings a publisher prints around amended words; square brackets are the commonest.
amendment_markers.title: Amendment Markers

font_preference.description: Preferred font style for display. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
font_preference.title: Font Preference

heading_case.description: How headings are cased. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
heading_case.title: Heading Case

heading_type.description: How provision headings are printed. Declaring `marginal_note` explicitly also scans for basic units whose heading is printed as a marginal note.
heading_type.title: Heading Type

rtl.description: Whether the script runs right to left. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
rtl.title: Rtl

script.description: The writing system of the jurisdiction's texts, which selects the script pack used for normalisation and marker matching.
script.title: Script

akn_element.description: The AKN document element for the class, such as `act`. `doc` or `statement` selects an open structure rather than the legislative hierarchy.
akn_element.title: Akn Element

akn_subtype.description: AKN subtype for the class. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
akn_subtype.title: Akn Subtype

authoritative_language.description: Authoritative language for this class, for legal systems whose classes are enacted in different languages. None falls back to the jurisdiction's.
authoritative_language.title: Authoritative Language

basic_unit.description: The element that carries the class's numbered provisions, such as `section` or `article`. It is given to the structurer and used by the anchor coverage check.
basic_unit.title: Basic Unit

bluebell_compatible.description: Whether the class can be expressed in Bluebell. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
bluebell_compatible.title: Bluebell Compatible

direct_effect.description: Whether instruments of this class apply without domestic transposition. Only a supranational jurisdiction may set it to true.
direct_effect.title: Direct Effect

extends.description: Another class of this jurisdiction whose fields this one lays over. One level.
extends.title: Extends

frbr_subtype.description: The FRBR subtype segment for the class's works, returned with the class by the MCP jurisdiction tools.
frbr_subtype.title: Frbr Subtype

hcontainers.description: Containers with no AKN element of their own, structured under a proxy keyword and renamed to `hcontainer` afterwards.
hcontainers.title: Hcontainers

hierarchy.description: The class's structural levels. Higher levels must come before the basic unit and its subdivisions.
hierarchy.title: Hierarchy

label.description: Display name of the class, such as "Act" or "Regulation".
label.title: Label

local_label.description: The class's name in the local language. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
local_label.title: Local Label

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

number_has_year_prefix.description: True where a printed serial may open with the instrument's year; a matching year prefix is kept out of the URI number.
number_has_year_prefix.title: Number Has Year Prefix

number_source.description: "title_identity" makes the URI number the title digest, never a stated serial, for classes whose serials repeat across issuers. "stated" uses the printed serial.
number_source.title: Number Source

prompt_variant.description: Name of a structuring prompt variant for the class. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
prompt_variant.title: Prompt Variant

search_rank.description: Rank of the class in the legal hierarchy, used to order a title search: higher outranks lower on a close match, and unset means no weighting. Ranks: 4 constitutional, 3 primary legislation, 2 executive decree, 1 subordinate regulation or decision, 0 implementing instructions.
search_rank.title: Search Rank

short_label.description: Compact label for the class in the interface and in PDF exports. Falls back to the title-cased doctype when unset.
short_label.title: Short Label

DocumentPlacedTable.description:
A table outside every provision, with the eIds it sits under (outermost
first) so a reader can place it and a subtree read can keep it.
DocumentPlacedTable.title: DocumentPlacedTable

DocumentProvision.title: DocumentProvision

DocumentProvisionBlock.description:
One row in a nested-provision tree (paragraph / subparagraph / …).

Carries its own number, optional heading, intro inline run, nested
blocks, and trailing wrap-up so renderers can present a hanging
numbered hierarchy rather than a flattened paragraph. `table` is set
(and everything else empty) when `akn_type == "table"`.
DocumentProvisionBlock.title: DocumentProvisionBlock

DocumentSection.description:
Hierarchical container, title / chapter / part / article / etc.

Holds child sections and provisions in their persisted `position` order.
Top-level provisions (those without an enclosing section) hang off the
`VersionDocument.provisions` list instead.
DocumentSection.title: DocumentSection

DocumentTable.description: An AKN `<table>`, eId-keyed like every other citable unit.
DocumentTable.title: DocumentTable

DocumentTableCell.description:
One `<th>`/`<td>`; `content` is the same inline AST as any other cell of
legal text, so refs/terms/citations inside a table cell still render.
DocumentTableCell.title: DocumentTableCell

applies_to.description: What the formula applies to. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
applies_to.title: Applies To

document_class.description: The doctype, or list of doctypes, the formula applies to. Unset applies it to every doctype.
document_class.title: Document Class

enacting_body_tlc.description: eId of the TLC entry naming the enacting body. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
enacting_body_tlc.title: Enacting Body Tlc

era.description: Label of the period the formula belongs to, recorded in the ingest log.
era.title: Era

from.description: First date the formula applies to, inclusive. A bounded formula is never applied to a document without a date.
from.title: From

instrument_type.description: The instrument type the formula belongs to. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
instrument_type.title: Instrument Type

language.description: Language of the formula's text. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
language.title: Language

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

position.description: Where the formula sits in the document. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
position.title: Position

text.description: Wording injected into the preamble as the enacting formula when the source has none. Text with an unfilled template slot is never injected.
text.title: Text

to.description: Last date the formula applies to, inclusive.
to.title: To

transliteration.description: A transliteration of the formula's text. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
transliteration.title: Transliteration

verified.description: Whether the wording has been checked against source documents. A verified formula is preferred over an unverified one that also matches.
verified.title: Verified

calendar_conversion.description: Conversion rule for a jurisdiction whose instruments are dated in a non-Gregorian calendar. FRBR URIs always use Gregorian dates (ADR 001), and this rule drives the conversion.

country_code.description: The country segment of minted FRBR URIs, where it differs from the jurisdiction code (a subdivision homed under its parent, for example).
country_code.title: Country Code

date_calendar.description: The calendar the jurisdiction's FRBR dates are given in. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
date_calendar.title: Date Calendar

date_calendar_note.description: Free-text note on `date_calendar`. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
date_calendar_note.title: Date Calendar Note

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

notes.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
notes.title: Notes

number_extraction.description: How an instrument number is found in the source. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
number_extraction.title: Number Extraction

number_format.description: How instrument numbers are written. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
number_format.title: Number Format

number_note.description: Free-text note on instrument numbering. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
number_note.title: Number Note

sample_uris.description: Example FRBR URIs for the jurisdiction. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
sample_uris.title: Sample Uris

title_identity.description: Declared where instruments carry no number and the title is the identity.

uri_patterns.description: FRBR work URI template per doctype, using `{year}` and `{number}`. A doctype without one gets the canonical default.
uri_patterns.title: Uri Patterns

akn_element.description: The AKN element the container corresponds to, where one exists. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
akn_element.title: Akn Element

bluebell_keyword.description: A Bluebell keyword for the container. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
bluebell_keyword.title: Bluebell Keyword

bluebell_proxy.description: The Bluebell keyword the structurer uses for this container before it is renamed.
bluebell_proxy.title: Bluebell Proxy

description.description: Free-text description of the container. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
description.title: Description

label.description: Display label for the container. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
label.title: Label

level.description: Where the container sits in the hierarchy. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
level.title: Level

local_term.description: Heading text that identifies the container: a proxy element whose heading starts with it, ignoring case, is renamed to an `hcontainer`.
local_term.title: Local Term

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

numbering.description: How the container is numbered. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
numbering.title: Numbering

position.description: Where the container appears in the document. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
position.title: Position

requires_postprocessing.description: Whether the proxy element is renamed to an `hcontainer` after structuring. False leaves it as the proxy element.
requires_postprocessing.title: Requires Postprocessing

akn_element.description: The AKN element this level becomes, such as `article` or `chapter`.
akn_element.title: Akn Element

akn_name.description: The element name a publisher's own AKN uses in hyphenated eIds for this level (`section` in `section-55-2`), where it differs from `akn_element`.
akn_name.title: Akn Name

bluebell_keyword.description: The Bluebell keyword for this level. Unset uses the AKN element name in capitals.
bluebell_keyword.title: Bluebell Keyword

captions.description: The closed caption vocabulary a `caption` level answers to.
captions.title: Captions

eid_abbrev.description: Overrides the element's canonical eId prefix. Set it only where the element cannot imply one (an hcontainer, or two local terms on one element) or where the publisher's own AKN uses another prefix.
eid_abbrev.title: Eid Abbrev

level.description: Where the level sits: `higher` containers, the single `basic` unit and its `subdivision`s are ordered; `grouping` and `presentational` levels may appear anywhere.
level.title: Level

local_term.description: The level's name as the source prints it, such as "Article" or "Chapter". Marker detection and the eId builder match it in the text.
local_term.title: Local Term

local_terms.description: The level's local names, keyed by ISO 639-3 language code, or by "script:<ISO 15924 code>" for a script variant.
local_terms.title: Local Terms

marker_form.description: For genres whose levels carry no keyword, such as a judgment that numbers its paragraphs "[1.1]" and never names the level. Unset keeps keyword matching.
marker_form.title: Marker Form

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

numbering.description: How the level is numbered, such as arabic or roman. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
numbering.title: Numbering

eli_base.description: Base URI of the jurisdiction's European Legislation Identifiers. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
eli_base.title: Eli Base

pattern.description: Pattern of identifiers in that scheme. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
pattern.title: Pattern

system.description: Name of the jurisdiction's own identifier scheme. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
system.title: System

InlineAnchor.description: Running text a citation can name, such as a recital.
InlineAnchor.title: InlineAnchor

InlineNote.description: A footnote bound to the provision it annotates, not part of its prose.
InlineNote.title: InlineNote

adoption_markers.description: Phrases declaring the instrument adopts another body's numbered text, which every count over the document must read as an attachment, not its own structure.
adoption_markers.title: Adoption Markers

akn_profile.description: Name of the AKN profile the jurisdiction's publisher uses. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
akn_profile.title: Akn Profile

akn_sources.description: Hand-curated list of upstream sources. Read alongside `source_adapters`; `effective_tier` considers both.
akn_sources.title: Akn Sources

attachments.description: Captions opening an attachment, whose numbering restarts the body's.
attachments.title: Attachments

authoritative_language.description: The language whose text is legally authoritative, used when a document's own language cannot be detected.
authoritative_language.title: Authoritative Language

binding_regimes.description: Non-membership binding regimes (treaty frameworks, bilateral regimes, constitutional annexes), which are not memberships.
binding_regimes.title: Binding Regimes

calendar.description: The calendar the jurisdiction's instruments are dated in.
calendar.title: Calendar

closing_phrases.description: `LegalEra.closing_phrases` for a jurisdiction that declares no eras. An era's own list wins where it declares one.
closing_phrases.title: Closing Phrases

core_tlcs.description: Recurring persons, bodies and concepts, written to a document's `references` block when the document refers to them by eId.
core_tlcs.title: Core Tlcs

coverage_status.description: Whether the jurisdiction has its own corpus: `in_scope`, `subsumed` into another jurisdiction's, `no_corpus` or `deferred`.
coverage_status.title: Coverage Status

default_document_class.description: The doctype used when no classification rule matches. It must be a key of `document_classes`.
default_document_class.title: Default Document Class

display.description: How the jurisdiction's texts are written and displayed.

document_classes.description: The instrument types the jurisdiction issues, keyed by doctype.
document_classes.title: Document Classes

effective_tier.description:
Tier actually achievable in the current environment.

Walks both `source_adapters` and the legacy `akn_sources`, taking the best
(lowest) tier. Token-gated entries with an unset env var are skipped unless the
source declares a `fallback_format`, whose tier contributes instead.
effective_tier.title: Effective Tier

enacting_formula_markers.description: Phrases showing the source carries its own enacting formula, so none is injected. Never a cut point: a phrase here may open the instrument, not close it.
enacting_formula_markers.title: Enacting Formula Markers

enacting_formulae.description: Enacting formulae to inject when the source carries none, chosen by doctype and date.
enacting_formulae.title: Enacting Formulae

footnote_markers.description: `LegalEra.footnote_markers` for a jurisdiction that declares no eras. An era's own list wins where it declares one.
footnote_markers.title: Footnote Markers

frbr.description: How the jurisdiction's FRBR URIs are minted.

furniture_inline_patterns.description: Page furniture that shares a line with real content, such as a portal credit or a stamped URL, so it is removed from the line rather than discarding the line. Narrower than `ocr_header_patterns`, which also matches the real title on page one.
furniture_inline_patterns.title: Furniture Inline Patterns

furniture_line_patterns.description: Page furniture whose whole line can be discarded: mastheads, page numbers, stamps. Narrower than `ocr_header_patterns`, which also carries the running title and so matches the real title on page one; only this set is safe for whole-line removal.
furniture_line_patterns.title: Furniture Line Patterns

identification.description: The jurisdiction's own identifier scheme. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.

languages.description: Languages of the jurisdiction's texts, as ISO 639-3 codes. Where there is only one, it is used for a document whose language is not detected.
languages.title: Languages

legal_eras.description: Drafting periods, so quality is reported per era rather than per corpus; empty means one undivided population. Distinct from `CalendarConversion.eras`, which is a regnal year table.
legal_eras.title: Legal Eras

lexicon_words.description: Legal vocabulary particular to this jurisdiction, folded into the language's word list when a page is scored. A term naming one jurisdiction is that jurisdiction's data, not the language's.
lexicon_words.title: Lexicon Words

members.description: For a supranational jurisdiction, the codes of its members. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
members.title: Members

min_anchor_coverage.description: Minimum ratio of captured structural anchors to marker literals in the source; ingest fails below it, so a partial AKN cannot ship. The default 0.80 tolerates in-prose cross-references, and 0.0 disables the check.
min_anchor_coverage.title: Min Anchor Coverage

name_local.description: The jurisdiction's name in its own language.
name_local.title: Name Local

name_translations.description: Localised jurisdiction names keyed by ISO 639-3 language code, used to render an export cover in the target language, in the same shape as a law's title translations.
name_translations.title: Name Translations

note.description: Free-text note at the jurisdiction level for cross-cutting guidance.
note.title: Note

numbering.description: How instruments are numbered and cited.

ocr_header_patterns.description: Running header and footer text that leaks into article bodies during OCR, stripped from paragraphs before translation so the model never sees it. Regex strings, so a profile author can add patterns without touching Python.
ocr_header_patterns.title: Ocr Header Patterns

opening_material_terminators.description: Phrases the recitals precede, after which any further pre-body text is stray page text.
opening_material_terminators.title: Opening Material Terminators

placeholders.description: Whole-string markers for missing or struck content, checked in addition to the built-in placeholder pattern.
placeholders.title: Placeholders

pool_excluded_refers_to.description: `refersTo` values marking a duty on someone other than the instrument's subjects. Units at or under a marked element stay readable but are not embedded or assessed.
pool_excluded_refers_to.title: Pool Excluded Refers To

public_reference.description: True where the config ships in the open core. Defaults to false, so a jurisdiction joins the open set only by a deliberate edit.
public_reference.title: Public Reference

residual_legal_systems.description: Foreign legal corpora still residually applicable here, such as pre-independence or occupying-power law left in force, so amendment and consolidation tooling can trace layered systems.
residual_legal_systems.title: Residual Legal Systems

segmentation.description: Where one source holds several instruments, how their openings are read.

source_adapters.description: Structured acquisition adapters for this jurisdiction, read by `codify.acquisition`.
source_adapters.title: Source Adapters

source_truncation_floor.description: Share of a document's contents listing that may lack a body before the source is treated as truncated. Off by default (0.0), since a threshold has to be set for each series from that series' own documents.
source_truncation_floor.title: Source Truncation Floor

status.description: How far the config has been validated, as listed in the registry.
status.title: Status

structuring.description: Settings for marker detection, classification and the structurer.

subsumed_by.description: The code of the jurisdiction whose corpus covers this one. Required when `coverage_status` is `subsumed` and refused otherwise.
subsumed_by.title: Subsumed By

supranational_memberships.description: Supranational bodies the jurisdiction belongs to. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
supranational_memberships.title: Supranational Memberships

synthetic.description: True for a fictional jurisdiction authored as synthetic test material. It is discovered and validated like any other config but kept out of the derived registry and the world atlas, which list real jurisdictions only.
synthetic.title: Synthetic

tier.description: Availability tier of the jurisdiction's statute base: 1 AKN native, 2 XML-structured, 3 HTML anchors, 4 PDF-only, 5 no online statute base.
tier.title: Tier

tradition.description: The legal traditions the jurisdiction draws on. At least one is required.
tradition.title: Tradition

type.description: Whether the jurisdiction is national, supranational, subnational or a crown dependency.
type.title: Type

validation.description: How far the config has been checked against real documents. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.

LawSummary.description: One law in a listing: its identity, FRBR work URI and latest expression date.
LawSummary.title: LawSummary

LegalEra.description:
A period whose documents share a drafting convention and authority.

Structural quality tracks era more than jurisdiction, so it is reported per era.
``from_``/``to`` are inclusive ISO dates, either may be open, and the field is
spelled ``from`` in the config files.

authority_patterns.description: How this era's offices are named in provision text, to flag provisions for review. A match means the office is named, not that it is granted a power; opt-in per era, since an era ending does not abolish its authorities.
authority_patterns.title: Authority Patterns

calendar.description: The calendar this era's instruments are dated in, where it differs from the jurisdiction's current one. None means it does not differ. Same closed set as the jurisdiction's own field, so the two cannot drift apart.
calendar.title: Calendar

closing_phrases.description: Phrases opening the attestation that closes a document of this era, so the promulgation and signature stop being read as the last article's text. Era-scoped because the wording follows the enacting authority.
closing_phrases.title: Closing Phrases

document_class.description: The document class typical of the era. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
document_class.title: Document Class

enacting_authority.description: The body that enacted instruments in this era. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
enacting_authority.title: Enacting Authority

footnote_markers.description: Regex for how a footnote marker opens in this era. The modern set uses superscripts and the older ones a parenthesised numeral; declaring only one form silently drops the other era.
footnote_markers.title: Footnote Markers

from.description: First date of the era, as an ISO date, inclusive. Unset leaves it open.
from.title: From

id.description: Identifier of the era, used to report structural quality per era.
id.title: Id

label.description: Display name of the era, given to the metadata extractor with its calendar.
label.title: Label

to.description: Last date of the era, as an ISO date, inclusive. Unset leaves it open.
to.title: To

LegalEra.title: LegalEra

act_citation.description: Citation pattern for acts. Reference resolution reads every `<class>_citation` field, and needs the default class's, to tell which instrument type a citation names.
act_citation.title: Act Citation

act_citation_alt.description: An alternative citation form for acts. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
act_citation_alt.title: Act Citation Alt

article_numbering.description: How articles are numbered. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
article_numbering.title: Article Numbering

citations.description: Citation pattern per instrument type, keyed by type, so a jurisdiction declares its own without a dedicated field for each.
citations.title: Citations

insertion_example.description: An example of an inserted unit's number. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
insertion_example.title: Insertion Example

insertion_note.description: Free-text note on how inserted units are numbered. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
insertion_note.title: Insertion Note

insertion_style.description: How inserted units are numbered. `slash_alpha` lets a marker number carry a slash and capital letter, as in "5/A".
insertion_style.title: Insertion Style

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

numbers_unique_across_years.description: Whether an instrument number identifies a work without its year. False for most jurisdictions, which restart numbering each year; true lets a year-less citation resolve on the number alone, and is a claim about the whole series, not just the documents held.
numbers_unique_across_years.title: Numbers Unique Across Years

series_citation_connectors.description: Regex fragments that may sit between a series name and its number.
series_citation_connectors.title: Series Citation Connectors

series_citations.description: Instruments cited by a never-reused series number and no year. Order matters: full names before abbreviations, so the full form wraps first.
series_citations.title: Series Citations

PlaceholderMarker.description:
A whole-string pattern a publisher writes where content is missing or
struck, and the AKN status the unit should carry for it.

pattern.description: Regex matched against a unit's whole text.
pattern.title: Pattern

status.description: The AKN `status` a unit matching `pattern` carries.

PlaceholderMarker.title: PlaceholderMarker

PlaceholderStatus.description:
The AKN `@status` a placeholder unit should carry; named so the generated
contract keeps a stable alias rather than a numbered `Status`.
PlaceholderStatus.title: PlaceholderStatus

ResidualLaw.description:
Another jurisdiction's corpus that is still residually applicable here.

Used for layered legal systems where historical residual law, law inherited
from a predecessor legal order, or foreign law continues in force alongside
native legislation. Examples:
  - another jurisdiction's law applied as a suppletive source.
  - a historical codification still applied to general private law.
  - an inherited common law (but usually too embedded to carve out as
        discrete residuals).

`source_jurisdiction` is a Codify code that must resolve to an existing
config. Downstream consolidation/amendment agents can traverse these to
find the source corpus.

in_force_from.description: Date the residual law began to apply.
in_force_from.title: In Force From

in_force_until.description: Date the residual law stopped applying.
in_force_until.title: In Force Until

label.description: Display name of the residual corpus.
label.title: Label

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

scope.description: What the residual law applies to: a territory, subjects, personal status or everything.
scope.title: Scope

source_jurisdiction.description: Code of the jurisdiction whose corpus applies. It must have a config.
source_jurisdiction.title: Source Jurisdiction

subjects.description: Subject areas the residual law applies to, when `scope` is subject_matter.
subjects.title: Subjects

superseded_by.description: Superseding acts (as FRBR URIs or free-text citations).
superseded_by.title: Superseded By

territories.description: Territories the residual law applies in, when `scope` is territorial.
territories.title: Territories

ResidualLaw.title: ResidualLaw

SegmentationConfig.description:
Lines that open an issue or an act, for telling apart the instruments one
source holds. Absent means the jurisdiction declares none, and nothing splits.

act_heading_patterns.description: Regexes matched at a line start; a `number` group, where present, is the label.
act_heading_patterns.title: Act Heading Patterns

contents_keywords.description: Headings of a contents listing, matched case-insensitively at a line start.
contents_keywords.title: Contents Keywords

issue_heading_patterns.description: The level above acts: a gazette issue within a bound volume.
issue_heading_patterns.title: Issue Heading Patterns

printed_page_pattern.description: A printed page number in a page's running header or footer; its first participating group is the number.
printed_page_pattern.title: Printed Page Pattern

skip_heading_patterns.description: Headings of instruments that are not acts (notices, appointments): kept apart, not ingested.
skip_heading_patterns.title: Skip Heading Patterns

trailing_section_patterns.description: Whole lines that open a trailing section which is never ingested: nothing is read from there on.
trailing_section_patterns.title: Trailing Section Patterns

SegmentationConfig.title: SegmentationConfig

SeriesCitation.description: A citation naming an instrument by series number alone ("Act No. 386").

doctype.description: The doctype whose FRBR work URI a matched citation links to.
doctype.title: Doctype

name.description: Regex for the instrument's name or abbreviation, matched case-insensitively.
name.title: Name

SeriesCitation.title: SeriesCitation

SourceAdapter.description:
One upstream portal for this jurisdiction; multiple permitted.

url_template placeholders: {country} {doctype} {year} {number} {frbr_uri}. Auth
tokens resolve from the env var named by auth_env_var, never stored here.

auth_env_var.description: Name of the environment variable holding the credential. The credential itself is never stored in the config.
auth_env_var.title: Auth Env Var

auth_scheme.description: How requests are authenticated. Anything but `none` needs `auth_env_var`.
auth_scheme.title: Auth Scheme

base_url.description: Root URL requests are made against. Unset uses the acquirer's default.
base_url.title: Base Url

discovery.description: How the source lists documents, for acquirers that support discovery.

licence.description: Licence the source publishes under, recorded on the documents it yields.
licence.title: Licence

name.description: Name of the source, used in log lines and errors.
name.title: Name

notes.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
notes.title: Notes

parser.description: Registered structured parser (in `codify.pipeline.parsers`) that converts this adapter's main body deterministically. None sends it through the general structuring lane.
parser.title: Parser

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Most requests per minute sent to the source's host. Unset leaves the acquirer's own default.
rate_limit_per_minute.title: Rate Limit Per Minute

robots_respect.description: Whether requests honour the host's robots.txt.
robots_respect.title: Robots Respect

url_template.description: Template for one document's URL, for acquirers that build it from the FRBR URI.
url_template.title: Url Template

SourceAdapter.title: SourceAdapter

body_opens_with_container.description: True where the drafting standard puts every article inside a container, so an article before the first one is a citation in the opening material. Some laws cite the constitution that way in the legal-basis recital.
body_opens_with_container.title: Body Opens With Container

citation_articles.description: Articles that may sit between the clause and the name (`the`). Language data: most languages have none, and no article is assumed.
citation_articles.title: Citation Articles

citation_lead_ins.description: Phrases introducing a law's own short name (`may be cited as`), the common-law short-title device.
citation_lead_ins.title: Citation Lead Ins

citation_subjects.description: How an instrument refers to itself when declaring its short name (`This Act`). Required with `citation_lead_ins`, because the same phrasing names bodies a law creates, and without it a law could take a school's or office's name as its own.
citation_subjects.title: Citation Subjects

citation_successors.description: Words that, following a marker's number on its own line, make the line a citation list rather than a provision ("Article 5 to Article 9 apply").
citation_successors.title: Citation Successors

classification_rules.description: Deterministic classification rules, evaluated in descending priority before the model is asked. `prompt_additions` carries only style hints the rules cannot express.
classification_rules.title: Classification Rules

designation_rule.description: Derives a short name from the title's own grammar where the legal tradition declares no short title. `eu_instrument` cites an act by its form and number.
designation_rule.title: Designation Rule

example_markers.description: Lead-ins that introduce specimen legislation in a drafting manual ("Example"), whose markers are displayed rather than enacted.
example_markers.title: Example Markers

insertion_suffixes.description: Words after a marker's number that mark an inserted unit ("5 bis"), mapped to the eId form. One shared table, like `ordinal_words`: never blank, a number, or a bare Latin letter.
insertion_suffixes.title: Insertion Suffixes

long_title_lead_ins.description: Openings of the document's own long title (`An Act`), marked up as `<longTitle>` so the official title comes from the text rather than from a filename.
long_title_lead_ins.title: Long Title Lead Ins

marker_boundary.description: `line_anchored` where the drafting standard puts the marker on its own line and the sources keep it, so a mid-sentence citation cannot anchor.
marker_boundary.title: Marker Boundary

marker_order.description: `number_first` where the number precedes the keyword (as in "15. §").
marker_order.title: Marker Order

marker_tolerances.description: OCR damage the sources carry, tolerated for this jurisdiction only so parsing elsewhere is unchanged. `missing_separator` accepts a keyword run into its number, as in "Article24".
marker_tolerances.title: Marker Tolerances

ordinal_words.description: Ordinal words used as container numbers (as in "Part One"). Declared in the source's own casing; matching is case-sensitive.
ordinal_words.title: Ordinal Words

prompt_additions.description: Jurisdiction-specific guidance appended to the structurer's context, for style hints the deterministic rules cannot express.
prompt_additions.title: Prompt Additions

prompt_variant.description: Name of a structuring prompt variant. Recorded for reference; the pipeline does not read it.
prompt_variant.title: Prompt Variant

prose_precursors.description: Words ending the previous line when a citation wraps onto the next, which a boundary rule cannot see. Empty falls back to the script pack's list.
prose_precursors.title: Prose Precursors

recurring_furniture.description: True where the layout engine files footnotes and page-top captions as header or footer, so only text repeated across pages counts as running header or footer, and a block opening on a marker is a note.
recurring_furniture.title: Recurring Furniture

reference_nouns.description: Words that introduce a citation's number ("Article 41 paragraph (3)"). A line ending in one makes the bracketed number on the next line part of the citation, not a marker opening a new provision.
reference_nouns.title: Reference Nouns

sameline_precursors.description: Precursors that mark a citation only when adjacent on the same line.
sameline_precursors.title: Sameline Precursors

body.description: Code of the body, canonicalised against the supranational body registry.
body.title: Body

direct_effect.description: How strongly the body's law takes effect, from override (strongest) to none. Legacy boolean values are read as "direct" or "none".
direct_effect.title: Direct Effect

direct_effect_instruments.description: The body's instrument types that have direct effect.
direct_effect_instruments.title: Direct Effect Instruments

excluded_instruments.description: Instruments of the body the member does not apply.
excluded_instruments.title: Excluded Instruments

excluded_subjects.description: Subject areas the member has opted out of.
excluded_subjects.title: Excluded Subjects

member_since.description: Date membership began, as a loose string, since some sources give only a year such as "1999".
member_since.title: Member Since

member_until.description: Date membership ended, as an ISO 8601 date; set only when status is "former".
member_until.title: Member Until

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

protocol_references.description: The treaties or protocols that create the carve-outs, as free text (for example "Protocol 21 TFEU").
protocol_references.title: Protocol References

rejoined_on.description: Date a former member rejoined after its membership lapsed; `member_since` keeps the original date.
rejoined_on.title: Rejoined On

superseded_subjects.description: Subject areas where the body's law displaces domestic law.
superseded_subjects.title: Superseded Subjects

suspension_periods.description: History of suspensions and reinstatements, including repeated cycles and a suspension still in force (`suspended_until` unset).
suspension_periods.title: Suspension Periods

transposition_required.description: Whether the body's instruments need transposing into national law: a boolean, or a list of the instrument types that do (for example ["directive"]).
transposition_required.title: Transposition Required

SuspensionPeriod.description:
One period of suspension from a supranational body.

Used inside `SupranationalMembership.suspension_periods` to record the
start and (optional) end of a suspension, plus its scope. A list is the
right shape because a jurisdiction can cycle through multiple suspensions.

reason.description: Why the suspension was imposed, as free text.
reason.title: Reason

scope.description: What the suspension withdraws: all rights, or only decision-making, voting or attendance at meetings. Defaults to full withdrawal.
scope.title: Scope

suspended_from.description: Start of the suspension, as an ISO 8601 date.
suspended_from.title: Suspended From

suspended_until.description: End of the suspension, as an ISO 8601 date; None while still suspended.
suspended_until.title: Suspended Until

SuspensionPeriod.title: SuspensionPeriod

class.description: The AKN TLC element the entry becomes, such as `TLCOrganization`.
class.title: Class

eId.description: An NCName-compatible identifier; camelCase and hyphenated forms are both accepted, and an empty one is refused.
eId.title: Eid

href.description: The URI the entry refers to, written to its `href` attribute.
href.title: Href

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

showAs.description: The display name written to the entry's `showAs` attribute.
showAs.title: Showas

TitleIdentity.description:
How a jurisdiction that numbers nothing derives an identity from a title.
Every field is a literal `codify.frbr.identity_from_title` reads.

consolidation_markers.description: Parenthetical words marking a re-publication; an edition number after one is the edition folded in, not this document's.
consolidation_markers.title: Consolidation Markers

edition_markers.description: Words inside a parenthetical naming this instrument's edition, spelling variants included; the first is canonical and is what a slug carries.
edition_markers.title: Edition Markers

strip_prefixes.description: Document-kind words opening a short title, longest first.
strip_prefixes.title: Strip Prefixes

year_particles.description: Words marking the year that follows as the instrument's own.
year_particles.title: Year Particles

ambiguities.description: The open questions about the config, as free text.
ambiguities.title: Ambiguities

bluebell_tested.description: Whether the config's structure has been tested through Bluebell.
bluebell_tested.title: Bluebell Tested

documents_examined.description: How many source documents the config was checked against.
documents_examined.title: Documents Examined

documents_examined_note.description: Free-text note on the documents examined.
documents_examined_note.title: Documents Examined Note

laws_africa_reference.description: Whether Laws.Africa covers this jurisdiction: a URL to its collection, or a bare flag.
laws_africa_reference.title: Laws Africa Reference

note.description: Free-text note for config authors. The pipeline does not read it.
note.title: Note

status.description: How far the config has been validated: `production`, `draft` or `stub`.
status.title: Status

unresolved_ambiguities.description: How many open questions about the config remain.
unresolved_ambiguities.title: Unresolved Ambiguities

VersionDocument.description: Full body of a single version, rendered as a tree.
VersionDocument.title: VersionDocument
